body:
maria: Hey, noticed a slow, steady memory climb on long streaming chat sessions (~6-12h). It correlates with sessions that keep tool-loop RPCs open. Heap growth ~150MB/hour on a 64GB instance. flamegraph + heapmap here: https://internal.gcs/reports/3332109876/heapmap.png

kai: can you paste the runtime/version + model?

maria: runtime v2.14.1 (kernel selector enabled), model: x-rlhf-13b-q4, continuous batching on, kv cache enabled with prefix caching. Repro job config: `--profile --longchat --tool-loop=on --session-ttl=24h`

sam: quick Q: is this the same leak we saw last month or different pattern?

maria: different imo. Last month was a sharp jump on canary restart. This is gradual and only for streams with repeated tool calls + intermittent short prefix reuse.

lee: any traces showing pinned pages? `kv_resident_pages` or slab stats?

maria: pasted abbreviated slab dump below:
```
KV_SLAB: total_pages=122304 resident=118900 pinned=4200 orphaned=12
page_age_hist: 0-1h: 25% 1-6h: 35% 6-24h: 30% 24h+: 10%
Pinned reasons: 70% active_kv_refs, 20% allocator_lock_hold, 10% unknown
```

juan: hmm pinned pages ~4200 is significant. Could be a missing eviction path when `toolloop` touch patterns keep prefixes in LRU. Any eviction logs?

maria: eviction log shows attempted evicts but SKIP due to `active_refs>0`. Excerpt:
```
[2026-03-10T04:12:01Z] evict_try: candidate=0x7fffee340 locked_refs=2 -> skip
[2026-03-10T04:12:01Z] evict_try: candidate=0x7fffcc210 locked_refs=1 -> skip
[2026-03-10T04:12:02Z] evict_scan: scanned=1200 freed=3
```

kai: could active_refs be referencing KV entries from callbacks in toolchain threads not releasing due to anomaly? we had one change around kernel selection to keep KV handles around longer for async AZ kernels.

maria: I tried reverting the PR locally (kernel-selection: keep-kv-on-async) and saw slower growth in a short run. Not conclusive.

lee: let's try a targeted repro: run a streaming chat with toolloop that reuses prefixes but includes a forced `kv_release()` between tool calls. If growth stops, it's a ref leak.

maria: scheduled a job `longchat-kv-refguard-3332` with `--force-kv-release` and added heap profiler. queued at ci.

ci-bot: Job queued: longchat-kv-refguard-3332 (runner: perf-cc-04), ETA 12m

sam: also check `allocator_backtrace` sampling around the time ref count goes up. Might point to thread that holds the ref.

maria: here's a sampling dump when resident pages were ~116k:
```
# top frames holding refs:
1) runtime::ToolLoop::handle_response (34%)
2) runtime::kv::PinGuard::acquire (28%)
3) grpc::CallContext::on_stream (12%)
4) kernel_selector::async_submit (8%)
```

lee: `ToolLoop::handle_response` + `PinGuard::acquire` strongly implies we keep pinned refs while processing tool callbacks. Are callbacks sometimes re-entrant?

maria: yes, tool handlers can call back into runtime to fetch embeddings for tool args — we suspected re-entrancy. The `PinGuard` is not re-entrant-safe.

juan: that is a smoking gun. If callbacks reacquire without releasing, refcount stays >0 and eviction never frees.

maria: patch idea: convert PinGuard to reentrant-aware (track owner thread id + recursive depth) OR detect if same thread trying to acquire and avoid increment. Quick patch bench looks promising.

kai: we should also add a defensive metric: `kv_pin_reentrant_detected` and an eviction amplifier that forces release on long-held pinned >30m.

megan: from product POV, how likely is this to impact customers? any public incidents?

maria: affects long-running streaming sessions with tool loops and nested runtime calls — relatively niche but high-impact for a few large customers running persistent assistants.

sam: test plan: 1) reproduce with forced nested callback, 2) run reentrant PinGuard patch in canary for 48h, 3) monitor slab/pinned pages + `kv_pin_reentrant_detected` counter, 4) revert if any correctness break.

maria: I'll open a PR with tests and a perf canary run. Attaching quick repro script snippet:
```bash
# reproduce: spawn streaming session that calls tool which triggers embedding request in handler
python tools/run_longchat.py --loops 1000 --call-backs nested --delay 0.1
```

lee: also add a microbench for kernel-selector path that kept KV alive to ensure no perf regression. Keep the patch small.

maria: noted. I'll link PR and canary results here once done. thx all :raised_hands:

juan: thanks — assigning to maria for ownership. I'll help watch the canary metrics.

maria: assigning: maria -> owner, juan -> oncall watcher, kai -> kernel selection context FYI

megan: ping me if customers ask, will draft a short internal note for account execs.

maria: last note: if anyone has similar longchat traces, paste them here. I want more samples before canary.
